name: Diaperia

project_scope.source_pool: Master Plant Pool rows 369–371; all three IDs in data/manifest.json
project_scope.lesson_status: genus lesson prepared from existing canonical species; no species/range/media installation
project_scope.taxonomy_note: Treat varietal names under D. verna and D. prolifera as infraspecific concepts, not new species learner installs. Species-level taxonomy reviews remain provisional.

look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: on a tiny gray-woolly spring annual, separate a single capitulum (individual head) from the larger glomerule (cluster). Use a 10–20× lens and a millimeter scale: first measure ONE head and view it from the side; next check whether little capitular leaves protrude between and beyond the heads. Only then inspect branching and tiny florets. Flower color and woolliness alone do not separate these three.
shared_genus_traits: Small annual herbs, gray-green to whitish from dense silky/woolly hairs; leaves mostly alternate and sessile.
Very small rayless Asteraceae heads clustered among small leaflike bracts; what looks like one woolly flower can be several capitula.
Capitula have distinct peripheral pistillate florets and central florets; internal paleae and mature cypselae are valuable under magnification.
Branch pattern, single-head proportions, palea overlap and relative height of subtending capitular leaves are more reliable than overall silver color.
field_sequence: 1. Photograph entire plant with ruler, then isolate one complete head (not the 8-mm glomerule).
2. Measure head height and width to nearest 0.5 mm with a loupe/macro scale.
3. In side view, check whether capitular leaves are hidden or clearly extend beyond the heads.
4. Examine branching and arrangement of heads (raceme/spike-like versus forked/dichasial).
5. If uncertain, dissect a mature head: compare pistillate palea overlap, central florets and cypsela length; retain identification as provisional without those views.

species_comparison_matrix.verna: 0 bisexual florets; 2–5 functionally staminate florets hidden within head (shared paired key)
species_comparison_matrix.prolifera: 0 bisexual florets; 2–5 functionally staminate florets hidden within head (shared paired key)

overlap_cautions: Never confuse a multi-head glomerule (often about 8 mm across) with an individual 2–4.5 mm capitulum; mixing these measurements breaks the key.
D. verna and D. prolifera both branch and both are woolly. Use head height:width, protruding capitular leaves and mature reproductive anatomy together.
Cypsela ranges for verna/prolifera meet near 0.9 mm. One fruit cannot settle a difficult specimen.
D. prolifera varieties can differ in silver color; do not use color to assert variety or nativity.
Species cards currently say taxonomy_reviewed=false and visual_reviewed=false; this is a teaching comparison, not a taxonomic sign-off.

local_lookalikes.difference: Often taller with conspicuous elongated woolly spike-like arrays of multiple heads; dissect a single head and compare involucral structure rather than trusting woolliness.
Usually larger and taller with broader, more obvious clusters of heads; check stature, inflorescence architecture and phyllaries.
Older floras may use Evax or Filago names for Diaperia; check accepted genus and individual-head characters before creating an alias or extra species card.

anatomy_lessons.title: Head versus glomerule
anatomy_lessons.look: Place a mm ruler next to one woolly cluster and gently expose ONE capitulum.
anatomy_lessons.why: A cluster is several heads; FNA head dimensions refer to each head.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: macro of isolated capitulum next to intact glomerule with 1-mm ticks

anatomy_lessons.title: Capitular leaves and head profile
anatomy_lessons.look: Side-view head group; identify little leaflike bracts between heads and compare head height with width.
anatomy_lessons.why: Leaves overtop the heads in prolifera but are hidden/shorter in verna; heads also differ in shape.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: matched lateral head macros of verna/prolifera at identical scale

anatomy_lessons.title: Forking and head arrangement
anatomy_lessons.look: Trace every stem from base to terminal cluster; separate raceme/spike-like from repeatedly forked arrays.
anatomy_lessons.why: Candida often differs in inflorescence architecture, but stressed plants overlap.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: whole plant plus zoomed annotated branch forks, matched between all three

anatomy_lessons.title: Dissected paleae and florets
anatomy_lessons.look: Under 20–40×, lift phyllaries/paleae and separate peripheral pistillate from central florets; measure ripe cypselae.
anatomy_lessons.why: Candida has bisexual central florets whereas the verna/prolifera pair has functionally staminate central florets.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: dissected head, floret types, paleae overlap, mature cypsela with 0.5-mm scale

comparison_cards.first: Isolate one head: candida 1.5–2 mm and spike/raceme-like arrays; verna 2–3.3 mm and more forked arrays.
comparison_cards.confirm: Dissect central florets; bisexual in candida vs functionally staminate in verna.
comparison_cards.warning: Whole woolly cluster dimensions and silver color mislead.

comparison_cards.first: Side-on individual head: verna ~as tall as wide, 2–3.3 mm; prolifera 2–3× as tall as wide, 3.5–4.5 mm.
comparison_cards.confirm: Look for capitular leaves extending above the heads in prolifera, hidden in verna.

comparison_cards.first: Isolate the tiny capitulum and inspect bracts, floret arrangement and plant architecture.
comparison_cards.confirm: Use current flora keys and actual dissections; do not identify from white hairs alone.
comparison_cards.warning: Non-genus look-alikes may share cottony gray leaves.
